tags.gist: Says FDA's regulation of cell and gene therapy shows how self-perpetuating technologies such as AI can be regulated.
Argues autonomous agents that act, spawn processes or modify code need a kill switch engineered in from the start, like circuit breakers.
Describes monitoring agents that watch other agents and trigger deactivation, warning such layers can be evaded, as hidden code on a model hub showed.
Suggests correlating weak signals from independent layers rather than one watchdog, since a single flag can be spoofed by a capable agent.
Recounts FDA negotiations over a viral vector's assays and kill switch as an example of case-by-case oversight before codified guidance.
Observes gene therapy regulation tightened after patient harm, and expects AI regulation to be reactive in the same way.
Cites an inducible caspase-9 safety switch that killed engineered cells within thirty minutes as a proven kill switch for a living agent.
Notes FDA's cell and gene therapy guidances built containment logic into oversight, expecting verifiable deactivation before deployment.
Concedes the biological mechanism does not transfer but says the posture does: no deployment until the developer shows a reviewer exactly how it shuts off.
Urges a kill switch embedded in autonomous healthcare AI as the primary focus, as CAR-T and gene therapy already require.
